method.title: Simulation assumptions and method
method.intro: This is an illustrative scenario based on unvalidated assumptions. It does not predict actual job displacement or reproduce a probability published by researchers.
method.event: Assumed event: demand for this occupation falls by at least {reduction} because of AI.
method.research: The input may use a US O*NET task exposure score from OpenAI research. That score is not a probability or date of employment loss.
method.basisOccupation: The unadjusted input {score} is this occupation’s task-exposure score from US O*NET research.
method.basisDefault: No occupation-specific research value is available, so the common reference value {score} is the unadjusted input.
method.probability: Illustrative cumulative probability after t years = 1 − exp(−λ × t)
method.time: A year is calculated as {days} days from baseline {baseline}. The timer shows when the illustrative cumulative probability reaches {threshold}.
method.limit: The coefficients, common value, event and timer threshold are arbitrary assumptions chosen by this site, not validated country-specific or individual employment forecasts.
scenario.basisNameProxy: Illustrative estimate based on occupation-name similarity; equivalence or official mapping is not established.
scenario.tieAdjustment: Code-based arbitrary adjustments create illustrative differences and resolve identical times; these are not research-verified differences.
method.basisNameProxy: The unadjusted input {score} is an unvalidated illustrative estimate based on similarity between Korean occupation names. Similar names do not establish equivalence or an official mapping.
method.tieAdjustment: Artificial crossing-time adjustment to resolve a duplicate time: {seconds} seconds. This is not a research-verified difference in risk.
method.effectiveScore: Actual formula input after all adjustments: {score}
method.syntheticDelta: Arbitrary code-based input variation used to create illustrative differences: {delta}. It is not a research result.
scenario.accelerated: The directly linked study’s task exposure exceeds {threshold}; this site applies a hypothetical {factor}× hazard rate. The study does not predict this displacement time.
method.accelerated: Only occupations with directly linked human-rated beta task exposure above {threshold} receive the site’s assumed {factor}× hazard rate. The study does not predict displacement timing or this multiplier.
method.medicalAcceleration: An additional {factor}× hazard is applied to physician, dentist and Korean medicine physician classifications as a requested scenario assumption. This timing is not predicted or validated by research.
method.governmentAdjustment: For senior central and local government officials, the hazard is multiplied by {factor} as a requested scenario assumption. This timing is not predicted or validated by research.
method.anthropicExact: Anthropic’s observed AI task exposure for US SOC occupation {code} is {score}. It is not an employment displacement probability.
method.anthropicGroup: Anthropic’s observed AI task exposure for the parent US SOC group {code} is {score}. It is not a measurement of this specialty alone or an employment displacement probability.
method.blsContext: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics projects {change}% employment change for the parent SOC group {code} from {baseline} to {horizon}. This figure does not separately estimate or attribute the effect of AI and is not an independent projection for the specialty.
detail.sharedClassification: Shared result for the official group “{name}”
method.timerV9: The baseline is {baseline}, with {days} days per year. The timer is a simulation adjusted separately from the illustrative displacement probability above. It is not a probability threshold or a date forecast by a research institution.
method.timerV9Assumptions: Timer coefficients are assumptions chosen by this site, not values validated by the reports. OpenAI task exposure and Anthropic observed exposure, which partly uses it, are not independent evidence and can reweight the same information. Task exposure is not a probability of employment displacement, and the US Bureau of Labor Statistics overall employment projection does not separately estimate or attribute the effect of AI.
method.timerV9Factor: The interval from the baseline to the earlier v8 simulation time is multiplied by {factor}. A value below 1 shortens the interval; a value above 1 lengthens it. A separate adjustment in seconds may be applied to avoid identical displayed times.
method.timerV9Robot: Anthropic robot task exposure index: O*NET {code}, source version {version}, {score} on the original 0–3 scale. The older classification and newer dataset are linked by the same code; this does not establish that their occupational scope is identical across versions. Robot capability is not actual adoption or a probability of employment displacement.
method.timerV10: The baseline is {baseline}, with {days} days per year. The timer and displayed probability use the same assumed model; neither is a date forecast by a research institution or an actual displacement probability.
method.timerV10Assumptions: The coefficients are assumptions chosen by this site, not values validated by the reports. OpenAI task exposure and Anthropic observed exposure, which partly uses it, are not independent evidence and can reweight the same information. Task exposure is not a probability of employment displacement, and the US Bureau of Labor Statistics overall employment projection does not separately estimate the effect of AI.
method.timerV10Collision: Artificial adjustment to distinguish identical displayed times: {seconds} seconds. This adjustment also affects the probability calculation and is not a research-verified difference.
